1: # Entire - CLI
2: 
3: This repo contains the CLI for Entire.
4: 
5: ## Architecture
6: 
7: - CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh
8: 
9: ## Key Directories
10: 
11: ### Commands (`cmd/`)
12: 
13: - `entire/`: Main CLI entry point. Also home to kubectl-style external-command resolution (`entire <name>` → `entire-<name>` on PATH) — see [External Commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md).
14: - `entire/cli`: CLI utilities and helpers (Cobra commands, helpers, group roots)
15: - `entire/cli/commands`: actual command implementations
16: - `entire/cli/agent`: agent implementations (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi) - see [Agent Integration Checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) and [Agent Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md)
17: - `entire/cli/strategy`: strategy implementation (manual-commit) - see section below
18: - `entire/cli/checkpoint`: checkpoint storage abstractions (temporary and committed)
19: - `entire/cli/session`: session state management
20: - `entire/cli/integration_test`: integration tests (simulated hooks)
21: - `e2e/`: E2E tests with real agent calls (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md))
22: 
23: ### Command Layout
24: 
25: The CLI is organized around five noun groups plus a small set of top-level
26: verbs. The groups are the canonical home for each verb; legacy top-level
27: shortcuts remain functional but hidden, and emit a deprecation hint pointing
28: at the canonical group form.
29: 
30: - `session` (alias: `sessions`): `list`, `info`, `stop`, `attach`, `resume`, `current`
31: - `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `explain`, `rewind`, `search`
32: - `agent`: bare opens the interactive agent selector, plus `list`, `add`, `remove`
33: - `configure`: bare prints help and a hint pointing at `entire agent`; flags
34:   manage non-agent settings (telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy
35:   options, summary provider). Agent CRUD lives under `entire agent`.
36: - `auth`: `login`, `logout`, `status`, `list`, `revoke`
37: - `doctor`: bare runs the scan-and-fix flow, plus `trace`, `logs`, `bundle`
38: 
39: Top-level lifecycle and standalone commands: `enable`, `disable`, `status`,
40: `login`, `logout`, `clean`, `version`, `dispatch`, `activity`, `help`,
41: `configure`.
42: 
43: Hidden top-level shortcuts (functional, emit a one-line deprecation hint):
44: `rewind` → `checkpoint rewind`, `resume` → `session resume`, `attach` →
45: `session attach`, `explain` → `checkpoint explain`, `trace` → `doctor trace`.
46: Cobra-native aliases (no hint): `sessions` → `session`, `cp`/`checkpoints` →
47: `checkpoint`. The `search` top-level remains hidden without a hint.
48: 
49: Deprecated top-level alias (functional, prints cobra deprecation message):
50: `reset` → `clean`.
51: 
52: Hidden infrastructure commands: `hooks`, `migrate`, `trail`,
53: `curl-bash-post-install`, `__send_analytics`.
54: 
55: The `hideAsAlias(cmd, canonical)` helper in `cmd/entire/cli/aliascmd.go`
56: marks a command Hidden and sets cobra's `Deprecated` field so the hint
57: renders to stderr on every invocation while the command stays functional.
58: Diagnostic subcommands live alongside `doctor.go` as `doctor_logs.go` and
59: `doctor_bundle.go`. Group roots and noun-group children live in files
60: named `<noun>_group.go` and `<noun>_<verb>.go` respectively.
61: 
62: ## Tech Stack
63: 
64: - Language: Go 1.26.x
65: - Build tool: mise, go modules
66: - Linting: golangci-lint
67: 
68: ## Development
69: 
70: ### Running Tests
71: 
72: ```bash
73: mise run test
74: ```
75: 
76: ### Running Integration Tests
77: 
78: ```bash
79: mise run test:integration
80: ```
81: 
82: ### Running All Tests (CI)
83: 
84: ```bash
85: mise run test:ci
86: ```
87: 
88: This runs unit tests, integration tests, and the E2E canary (Vogon agent) in sequence. Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.
89: 
90: ### Running E2E Canary Tests (Vogon Agent)
91: 
92: The Vogon agent is a deterministic fake agent that exercises the full E2E test suite without making any API calls. Named after the Vogons from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy — bureaucratic, procedural, and deterministic to a fault.
93: 
94: ```bash
95: mise run test:e2e:canary           # Run all E2E tests with the Vogon agent
96: mise run test:e2e:canary TestFoo   # Run a specific test
97: ```
98: 
99: - **Runs as part of `test:ci`** — canary failures block merges
100: - **No API calls, no cost** — safe to run freely, unlike real agent E2E tests
101: - **If a canary test fails, the bug is in the CLI or test infrastructure**, not in an agent
102: - Located in `e2e/vogon/` (binary) and `cmd/entire/cli/agent/vogon/` (Agent interface)
103: - The binary parses prompts via regex, creates/modifies/deletes files, and fires lifecycle hooks
104: - **IMPORTANT: When changing E2E test prompt wording**, the Vogon binary (`e2e/vogon/main.go`) parses prompts with hardcoded regexes. New phrasing may not match existing patterns — always run `mise run test:e2e:canary` after changing prompt text and fix Vogon's parsing if tests fail.
105: 
106: ### Running E2E Tests (Only When Explicitly Requested)
107: 
108: **IMPORTANT: Do NOT run E2E tests proactively.** E2E tests make real API calls to agents, which consume tokens and cost money. Only run them when the user explicitly asks for E2E testing.
109: 
110: ```bash
111: mise run test:e2e [filter]                          # All agents, filtered
112: mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code [filter]       # Claude Code only
113: mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli [filter]        # Gemini CLI only
114: mise run test:e2e --agent opencode [filter]          # OpenCode only
115: mise run test:e2e --agent cursor [filter]            # Cursor only
116: mise run test:e2e --agent factoryai-droid [filter]   # Factory AI Droid only
117: mise run test:e2e --agent copilot-cli [filter]       # Copilot CLI only
118: mise run test:e2e --agent pi [filter]                # Pi only
119: ```
120: 
121: E2E tests:
122: 
123: - Use the `//go:build e2e` build tag
124: - Located in `e2e/tests/`
125: - See [`e2e/README.md`](e2e/README.md) for full documentation (structure, debugging, adding agents)
126: - Test real agent interactions (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi, or Vogon creating files, committing, etc.)
127: - Validate checkpoint scenarios documented in `docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md`
128: - Support multiple agents via `E2E_AGENT` env var (`claude-code`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, `copilot-cli`, `pi`, `vogon`)
129: 
130: **Environment variables:**
131: 
132: - `E2E_AGENT` - Agent to test with (default: `claude-code`)
133: - `E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` - Claude model to use (default: `haiku` for cost efficiency)
134: - `E2E_TIMEOUT` - Timeout per prompt (default: `2m`)
135: 
136: ### Test Parallelization
137: 
138: **Always use `t.Parallel()` in tests.** Every top-level test function and subtest should call `t.Parallel()` unless it modifies process-global state (e.g., `os.Chdir()`).
139: 
140: ```go
141: func TestFeature_Foo(t *testing.T) {
142:     t.Parallel()
143:     // ...
144: }
145: 
146: // Integration tests with TestEnv
147: func TestFeature_Bar(t *testing.T) {
148:     t.Parallel()
149:     env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
150:     // ...
151: }
152: ```
153: 
154: **Exception:** Tests that modify process-global state cannot be parallelized. This includes `os.Chdir()`/`t.Chdir()` and `os.Setenv()`/`t.Setenv()` — Go's test framework will panic if these are used after `t.Parallel()`.
155: 
156: ### Git in Tests
157: 
158: **Tests that touch git state must use an isolated temp repo — never the real repo CWD.**
159: 
160: Many handlers (lifecycle, strategy, hooks) resolve the git repo from CWD via `OpenRepository`, `GetGitCommonDir`, `DetectFileChanges`, etc. Without isolation, tests can create session state files, shadow branches, or other artifacts in the real `.git/` directory.
161: 
162: Use the `testutil` helpers:
163: 
164: ```go
165: tmpDir := t.TempDir()
166: testutil.InitRepo(t, tmpDir)                    // git init + user config + disable GPG
167: testutil.WriteFile(t, tmpDir, "f.txt", "init")  // create a file
168: testutil.GitAdd(t, tmpDir, "f.txt")             // stage it
169: testutil.GitCommit(t, tmpDir, "init")           // commit (needs at least one commit for HEAD)
170: t.Chdir(tmpDir)                                 // redirect CWD-based git resolution
171: ```
172: 
173: `testutil.InitRepo` configures `user.name`, `user.email`, and disables GPG signing — safe for CI environments without global git config.
174: 
175: **Prefer `testutil.InitRepo()` over direct `git.PlainInit()` in tests.** When a test in this repo needs an initialized repository, use `testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)` unless the test specifically needs lower-level initialization behavior that the helper cannot provide. Do not call `git.PlainInit()` directly and then create commits or run CLI git operations without also reproducing the helper's repo-local config.
176: 
177: **Do NOT** shell out to `git init`/`git commit` directly without setting user config and `--no-gpg-sign`, and **do NOT** run lifecycle/strategy handlers from the real repo CWD in tests.
178: 
179: ### Spawning subprocesses in tests (TTY detection)
180: 
181: Tests that spawn the real `entire` or `git` binary need the child to be non-interactive so prompts don't hang on a developer terminal.
182: 
183: `interactive.CanPromptInteractively()` resolves in this order:
184: 
185: 1. `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1` → force interactive ON (any other non-empty value → force OFF).
186: 2. `testing.Testing()` → false. In-process `go test` runs are non-interactive by default; no per-test `t.Setenv("ENTIRE_TEST_TTY", "0")` is needed.
187: 3. Agent sentinels (`GEMINI_CLI`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `PI_CODING_AGENT`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`) → false.
188: 4. `CI=<non-empty-non-false>` → false.
189: 5. `/dev/tty` probe.
190: 
191: For subprocesses spawning the real `entire` binary (e2e, integration tests, `entire` calling itself from a hook), prefer `execx.NonInteractive` over env-var plumbing:
192: 
193: ```go
194: import "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/execx"
195: 
196: cmd := execx.NonInteractive(ctx, getTestBinary(), "status")
197: cmd.Dir = repoDir
198: out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
199: ```
200: 
201: `execx.NonInteractive` puts the child in a new session with no controlling terminal (`Setsid` on Unix, `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` on Windows), so the child's `/dev/tty` probe fails naturally. No env var required.
202: 
203: `interactive.UnderTest()` returns true when `testing.Testing()` or `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY` is set — use it where code needs to skip a real-terminal operation even if `CanPromptInteractively()` returns true (e.g., reading from `/dev/tty` directly inside `askConfirmTTY`).
204: 
205: ### Linting and Formatting
206: 
207: ```bash
208: mise run fmt && mise run lint
209: ```
210: 
211: `mise run fmt` can rewrite files. Treat `mise run fmt && mise run lint` as a single verification sequence: if formatting changes anything, run lint again on the formatted tree rather than assuming a previous lint result still applies.
212: 
213: ### Before Every Commit (REQUIRED)
214: 
215: **CI will fail if you skip these steps:**
216: 
217: ```bash
218: mise run check
219: ```
220: 
221: Equivalent expanded form:
222: 
223: ```bash
224: mise run fmt      # Format code (CI enforces gofmt)
225: mise run lint     # Lint check (CI enforces golangci-lint)
226: mise run test:ci  # Run all tests (unit + integration)
227: ```
228: 
229: `mise run check` runs the three commands above.
230: 
231: Safety note: do not treat a clean `mise run lint` result as final unless it was run after the most recent `mise run fmt` pass.
232: 
233: ### Before Any Push Or Remote Code Update (REQUIRED)
234: 
235: Before pushing commits or otherwise sending code changes to any remote, run `mise run lint` on the current tree and ensure it passes. If `mise run fmt` changed files, rerun `mise run lint` on the formatted tree before pushing.
236: 
237: **Common CI failures from skipping this:**
238: 
239: - `gofmt` formatting differences → run `mise run fmt`
240: - Lint errors → run `mise run lint` and fix issues
241: - Test failures → run `mise run test` and fix
242: 
243: ### Code Duplication Prevention
244: 
245: Before implementing Go code, use `/go:discover-related` to find existing utilities and patterns that might be reusable.
246: 
247: **Check for duplication:**
248: 
249: ```bash
250: mise run dup           # Comprehensive check (threshold 50) with summary
251: mise run dup:staged    # Check only staged files
252: mise run lint          # Normal lint includes dupl at threshold 75 (new issues only)
253: mise run lint:full     # All issues at threshold 75
254: ```
255: 
256: **Tiered thresholds:**
257: 
258: - **75 tokens** (lint/CI) - Blocks on serious duplication (~20+ lines)
259: - **50 tokens** (dup) - Advisory, catches smaller patterns (~10+ lines)
260: 
261: When duplication is found:
262: 
263: 1. Check if a helper already exists in `common.go` or nearby utility files
264: 2. If not, consider extracting the duplicated logic to a shared helper
265: 3. If duplication is intentional (e.g., test setup), add a `//nolint:dupl` comment with explanation
266: 
267: ## Code Patterns
268: 
269: ### Error Handling
270: 
271: The CLI uses a specific pattern for error output to avoid duplication between Cobra and main.go.
272: 
273: **How it works:**
274: 
275: - `root.go` sets `SilenceErrors: true` globally - Cobra never prints errors
276: - `main.go` prints errors to stderr, unless the error is a `SilentError`
277: - Commands return `NewSilentError(err)` when they've already printed a custom message
278: 
279: **When to use `SilentError`:**
280: Use `NewSilentError()` when you want to print a custom, user-friendly error message instead of the raw error:
281: 
282: ```go
283: // In a command's RunE function:
284: if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(); err != nil {
285:     cmd.SilenceUsage = true  // Don't show usage for prerequisite errors
286:     fmt.Fprintln(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Not a git repository. Please run 'entire enable' from within a git repository.")
287:     return NewSilentError(errors.New("not a git repository"))
288: }
289: ```
290: 
291: **When NOT to use `SilentError`:**
292: For normal errors where the default error message is sufficient, just return the error directly. main.go will print it:
293: 
294: ```go
295: // Normal error - main.go will print "unknown strategy: foo"
296: return fmt.Errorf("unknown strategy: %s", name)
297: ```
298: 
299: **Key files:**
300: 
301: - `errors.go` - Defines `SilentError` type and `NewSilentError()` constructor
302: - `root.go` - Sets `SilenceErrors: true` on root command
303: - `main.go` - Checks for `SilentError` before printing
304: 
305: ### Settings
306: 
307: All settings access should go through the `settings` package (`cmd/entire/cli/settings/`).
308: 
309: **Why a separate package:**
310: The `settings` package exists to avoid import cycles. The `cli` package imports `strategy`, so `strategy` cannot import `cli`. The `settings` package provides shared settings loading that both can use.
311: 
312: **Usage:**
313: 
314: ```go
315: import "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/settings"
316: 
317: // Load full settings object
318: s, err := settings.Load()
319: if err != nil {
320:     // handle error
321: }
322: if s.Enabled {
323:     // ...
324: }
325: 
326: // Or use convenience functions
327: if settings.IsSummarizeEnabled() {
328:     // ...
329: }
330: ```
331: 
332: **Do NOT:**
333: 
334: - Read `.entire/settings.json` or `.entire/settings.local.json` directly with `os.ReadFile`
335: - Duplicate settings parsing logic in other packages
336: - Create new settings helpers without adding them to the `settings` package
337: 
338: **Key files:**
339: 
340: - `settings/settings.go` - `EntireSettings` struct, `Load()`, and helper methods
341: - `config.go` - Higher-level config functions that use settings (for `cli` package consumers)
342: 
343: ### Logging vs User Output
344: 
345: - **Internal/debug logging**: Use `logging.Debug/Info/Warn/Error(ctx, msg, attrs...)` from `cmd/entire/cli/logging/`. Writes to `.entire/logs/`.
346: - **Enabling debug/perf logs locally**: Prefer adding `"log_level": "DEBUG"` to `.entire/settings.local.json` when you need detailed hook/perf logs. This file is gitignored, so it is a low-risk local-only change. `ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug` also works and takes precedence.
347: - **User-facing output**: Use `fmt.Fprint*(cmd.OutOrStdout(), ...)` or `cmd.ErrOrStderr()`.
348: 
349: Don't use `fmt.Print*` for operational messages (checkpoint saves, hook invocations, strategy decisions) - those should use the `logging` package.
350: 
351: **Privacy**: Don't log user content (prompts, file contents, commit messages). Log only operational metadata (IDs, counts, paths, durations).
352: 
353: ### Git Operations
354: 
355: We use github.com/go-git/go-git for most git operations, but with important exceptions:
356: 
357: #### go-git v5 Bugs - Use CLI Instead
358: 
359: **Do NOT use go-git v5 for `checkout` or `reset --hard` operations.**
360: 
361: go-git v5 has a bug where `worktree.Reset()` with `git.HardReset` and `worktree.Checkout()` incorrectly delete untracked directories even when they're listed in `.gitignore`. This would destroy `.entire/` and `.worktrees/` directories.
362: 
363: Use the git CLI instead:
364: 
365: ```go
366: // WRONG - go-git deletes ignored directories
367: worktree.Reset(&git.ResetOptions{
368:     Commit: hash,
369:     Mode:   git.HardReset,
370: })
371: 
372: // CORRECT - use git CLI
373: cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "reset", "--hard", hash.String())
374: ```
375: 
376: See `HardResetWithProtection()` in `common.go` and `CheckoutBranch()` in `git_operations.go` for examples.
377: 
378: Regression tests in `hard_reset_test.go` verify this behavior - if go-git v6 fixes this issue, those tests can be used to validate switching back.
379: 
380: #### Repo Root vs Current Working Directory
381: 
382: **Always use repo root (not `os.Getwd()`) when working with git-relative paths.**
383: 
384: Git commands like `git status` and `worktree.Status()` return paths relative to the **repository root**, not the current working directory. When an agent runs from a subdirectory (e.g., `/repo/frontend`), using `os.Getwd()` to construct absolute paths will produce incorrect results for files in sibling directories.
385: 
386: ```go
387: // WRONG - breaks when running from subdirectory
388: cwd, _ := os.Getwd()  // e.g., /repo/frontend
389: absPath := filepath.Join(cwd, file)  // file="api/src/types.ts" → /repo/frontend/api/src/types.ts (WRONG)
390: 
391: // CORRECT - use repo root
392: repoRoot, _ := paths.WorktreeRoot()
393: absPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, file)  // → /repo/api/src/types.ts (CORRECT)
394: ```
395: 
396: This also affects path filtering. The `paths.ToRelativePath()` function rejects paths starting with `..`, so computing relative paths from cwd instead of repo root will filter out files in sibling directories:
397: 
398: ```go
399: // WRONG - filters out sibling directory files
400: cwd, _ := os.Getwd()  // /repo/frontend
401: relPath := paths.ToRelativePath("/repo/api/file.ts", cwd)  // returns "" (filtered out as "../api/file.ts")
402: 
403: // CORRECT - keeps all repo files
404: repoRoot, _ := paths.WorktreeRoot()
405: relPath := paths.ToRelativePath("/repo/api/file.ts", repoRoot)  // returns "api/file.ts"
406: ```
407: 
408: **When to use `os.Getwd()`:** Only when you actually need the current directory (e.g., finding agent session directories that are cwd-relative).
409: 
410: **When to use repo root:** Any time you're working with paths from git status, git diff, or any git-relative file list.
411: 
412: Test case in `state_test.go`: `TestFilterAndNormalizePaths_SiblingDirectories` documents this bug pattern.
413: 
414: ### Session Strategy (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/`)
415: 
416: The CLI uses a manual-commit strategy for managing session data and checkpoints. The strategy implements the `Strategy` interface defined in `strategy.go`.
417: 
418: #### Strategy Interface
419: 
420: The `Strategy` interface provides:
421: 
422: - `SaveStep()` - Save session step checkpoint (code + metadata)
423: - `SaveTaskStep()` - Save subagent task step checkpoint
424: - `GetRewindPoints()` / `Rewind()` - List and restore to checkpoints
425: - `GetSessionLog()` / `GetSessionInfo()` - Retrieve session data
426: - `ListSessions()` / `GetSession()` - Session discovery
427: 
428: #### How It Works
429: 
430: The manual-commit strategy (`manual_commit*.go`) does not modify the active branch - no commits are created on the working branch. Instead it:
431: 
432: - Creates shadow branch `entire/<HEAD-commit-hash[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>` per base commit + worktree
433: - **Worktree-specific branches** - each git worktree gets its own shadow branch namespace, preventing conflicts
434: - **Supports multiple concurrent sessions** - checkpoints from different sessions in the same directory interleave on the same shadow branch
435: - Condenses session logs to permanent `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch on user commits
436: - Uses the `post-rewrite` Git hook to keep local session linkage aligned after amend/rebase rewrites
437: - Builds git trees in-memory using go-git plumbing APIs
438: - Rewind restores files from shadow branch commit tree (does not use `git reset`)
439: - **Location-independent transcript resolution** - transcript paths are always computed dynamically from the current repo location (via `agent.GetSessionDir` + `agent.ResolveSessionFile`), never stored in checkpoint metadata. This ensures restore/rewind works after repo relocation or across machines.
440: - **Copilot token scoping** - Copilot CLI `session.shutdown` contains session-wide token aggregates. Checkpoint metadata must stay scoped to `CheckpointTranscriptStart`; condensation may separately backfill full-session Copilot totals into session state for `entire status`.
441: - Tracks session state in `.git/entire-sessions/` (shared across worktrees)
442: - **Shadow branch migration** - if user does stash/pull/rebase (HEAD changes without commit), shadow branch is automatically moved to new base commit
443: - **Orphaned branch cleanup** - if a shadow branch exists without a corresponding session state file, it is automatically reset when a new session starts
444: - PrePush hook can push `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch alongside user pushes
445: - Safe to use on main/master since it never modifies commit history
446:

480: #### Session Phase State Machine
481: 
482: Sessions track their lifecycle through phases managed by a state machine in `session/phase.go`:
483: 
484: **Phases:** `ACTIVE`, `IDLE`, `ENDED`
485: 
486: **Events:**
487: 
488: - `TurnStart` - Agent begins a turn (UserPromptSubmit hook)
489: - `TurnEnd` - Agent finishes a turn (Stop hook)
490: - `GitCommit` - A git commit was made (PostCommit hook)
491: - `SessionStart` - New session started
492: - `SessionStop` - Session explicitly stopped
493: 
494: **Key transitions:**
495: 
496: - `IDLE + TurnStart → ACTIVE` - Agent starts working
497: - `ACTIVE + TurnEnd → IDLE` - Agent finishes turn
498: - `ACTIVE + GitCommit → ACTIVE` - User commits while agent is working (condense immediately)
499: - `IDLE + GitCommit → IDLE` - User commits between turns (condense immediately)
500: - `ENDED + GitCommit → ENDED` - Post-session commit (condense if files touched)
501: 
502: The state machine emits **actions** (e.g., `ActionCondense`, `ActionUpdateLastInteraction`) that hook handlers dispatch to strategy-specific implementations.
503: 
504: #### Metadata Structure
505: 
506: **Shadow branches** (`entire/<commit-hash[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`):
507: 
508: ```
509: .entire/metadata/<session-id>/
510: ├── full.jsonl               # Session transcript
511: ├── prompt.txt               # Checkpoint-scoped user prompts
512: └── tasks/<tool-use-id>/     # Task checkpoints
513:     ├── checkpoint.json      # UUID mapping for rewind
514:     └── agent-<id>.jsonl     # Subagent transcript
515: ```
516: 
517: **Metadata branch** (`entire/checkpoints/v1`) - sharded checkpoint format:
518: 
519: ```
520: <checkpoint-id[:2]>/<checkpoint-id[2:]>/
521: ├── metadata.json            # CheckpointSummary (aggregated stats)
522: ├── 0/                       # First session (0-based indexing)
523: │   ├── metadata.json        # Session-specific metadata
524: │   ├── full.jsonl           # Session transcript
525: │   ├── prompt.txt           # Checkpoint-scoped user prompts
526: │   ├── content_hash.txt     # SHA256 of transcript
527: │   └── tasks/<tool-use-id>/ # Task checkpoints (if applicable)
528: │       ├── checkpoint.json  # UUID mapping
529: │       └── agent-<id>.jsonl # Subagent transcript
530: ├── 1/                       # Second session (if multiple sessions)
531: │   ├── metadata.json
532: │   ├── full.jsonl
533: │   └── ...
534: └── ...
535: ```
536: 
537: **Multi-session metadata.json format:**
538: 
539: ```json
540: {
541:   "checkpoint_id": "abc123def456",
542:   "session_id": "2026-01-13-uuid", // Current/latest session
543:   "session_ids": ["2026-01-13-uuid1", "2026-01-13-uuid2"], // All sessions
544:   "session_count": 2, // Number of sessions in this checkpoint
545:   "strategy": "manual-commit",
546:   "created_at": "2026-01-13T12:00:00Z",
547:   "files_touched": ["file1.txt", "file2.txt"] // Merged from all sessions
548: }
549: ```
550: 
551: When multiple sessions are condensed to the same checkpoint (same base commit):
552: 
553: - Sessions are stored in numbered subfolders using 0-based indexing (`0/`, `1/`, `2/`, etc.)
554: - Latest session is always in the highest-numbered folder
555: - `session_ids` array tracks all sessions, `session_count` increments
556: 
557: **Session State** (filesystem, `.git/entire-sessions/`):
558: 
559: ```
560: <session-id>.json            # Active session state (base_commit, checkpoint_count, etc.)
561: ```
562: 
563: #### Checkpoint ID Linking
564: 
565: The strategy uses a **12-hex-char random checkpoint ID** (e.g., `a3b2c4d5e6f7`) as the stable identifier linking user commits to metadata.
566: 
567: **How checkpoint IDs work:**
568: 
569: 1. **Generated once per checkpoint**: When condensing session metadata to the metadata branch
570: 
571: 2. **Added to user commits** via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer:
572:    - **Manual-commit**: Added via `prepare-commit-msg` hook (user can remove it before committing)
573: 
574: 3. **Used for directory sharding** on `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch:
575:    - Path format: `<id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/`
576:    - Example: `a3b2c4d5e6f7` → `a3/b2c4d5e6f7/`
577:    - Creates 256 shards to avoid directory bloat
578: 
579: 4. **Appears in commit subject** on `entire/checkpoints/v1` commits:
580:    - Format: `Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7`
581:    - Makes `git log entire/checkpoints/v1` readable and searchable
582: 
583: **Bidirectional linking:**
584: 
585: ```
586: User commit → Metadata:
587:   Extract "Entire-Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7" trailer
588:   → Read a3/b2c4d5e6f7/ directory from entire/checkpoints/v1 tree at HEAD
589: 
590: Metadata → User commits:
591:   Given checkpoint ID a3b2c4d5e6f7
592:   → Search user branch history for commits with "Entire-Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7" trailer
593: ```
594: 
595: Note: Commit subjects on `entire/checkpoints/v1` (e.g., `Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7`) are
596: for human readability in `git log` only. The CLI always reads from the tree at HEAD.
597: 
598: **Example:**
599: 
600: ```
601: User's commit (on main branch):
602:   "Implement login feature
603: 
604:   Entire-Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7"
605:        ↓ ↑
606:        Linked via checkpoint ID
607:        ↓ ↑
608: entire/checkpoints/v1 commit:
609:   Subject: "Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7"
610: 
611:   Tree: a3/b2c4d5e6f7/
612:     ├── metadata.json (checkpoint_id: "a3b2c4d5e6f7")
613:     ├── full.jsonl (session transcript)
614:     └── prompt.txt
615: ```
616: 
617: #### Commit Trailers
618: 
619: **On user's active branch commits:**
620: 
621: - `Entire-Checkpoint: <checkpoint-id>` - 12-hex-char ID linking to metadata on `entire/checkpoints/v1`
622:   - Added via `prepare-commit-msg` hook; user can remove it before committing to skip linking
623: 
624: **On shadow branch commits (`entire/<commit-hash[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`):**
625: 
626: - `Entire-Session: <session-id>` - Session identifier
627: - `Entire-Metadata: <path>` - Path to metadata directory within the tree
628: - `Entire-Task-Metadata: <path>` - Path to task metadata directory (for task checkpoints)
629: - `Entire-Strategy: manual-commit` - Strategy that created the commit
630: 
631: **On metadata branch commits (`entire/checkpoints/v1`):**
632: 
633: Commit subject: `Checkpoint: <checkpoint-id>` (or custom subject for task checkpoints)
634: 
635: Trailers:
636: 
637: - `Entire-Session: <session-id>` - Session identifier
638: - `Entire-Strategy: <strategy>` - Strategy name (manual-commit)
639: - `Entire-Agent: <agent-name>` - Agent name (optional, e.g., "Claude Code")
640: - `Ephemeral-branch: <branch>` - Shadow branch name (optional)
641: - `Entire-Metadata-Task: <path>` - Task metadata path (optional, for task checkpoints)
642: 
643: **Note:** The strategy keeps active branch history clean - the only addition to user commits is the single `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. It never creates commits on the active branch (the user creates them manually). All detailed session data (transcripts, prompts, context) is stored on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` orphan branch or shadow branches.
644: 
645: #### Multi-Session Behavior
646: 
647: **Concurrent Sessions:**
648: 
649: - When a second session starts in the same directory while another has uncommitted checkpoints, a warning is shown
650: - Both sessions can proceed - their checkpoints interleave on the same shadow branch
651: - Each session's `RewindPoint` includes `SessionID` and `SessionPrompt` to help identify which checkpoint belongs to which session
652: - On commit, all sessions are condensed together with archived sessions in numbered subfolders
653: - Note: Different git worktrees have separate shadow branches (worktree-specific naming), so concurrent sessions in different worktrees do not conflict
654: 
655: **Orphaned Shadow Branches:**
656: 
657: - A shadow branch is "orphaned" if it exists but has no corresponding session state file
658: - This can happen if the state file is manually deleted or lost
659: - When a new session starts with an orphaned branch, the branch is automatically reset
660: - If the existing session DOES have a state file (concurrent session in same directory), a `SessionIDConflictError` is returned
661: 
662: **Shadow Branch Migration (Pull/Rebase):**
663: 
664: - If user does stash → pull → apply (or rebase), HEAD changes but work isn't committed
665: - The shadow branch would be orphaned at the old commit
666: - Detection: base commit changed AND old shadow branch still exists (would be deleted if user committed)
667: - Action: shadow branch is renamed from `entire/<old-hash>-<worktreeHash>` to `entire/<new-hash>-<worktreeHash>`
668: - Session continues seamlessly with checkpoints preserved
669: 
670: #### When Modifying the Strategy
671: 
672: - The strategy must implement the full `Strategy` interface
673: - Test with `mise run test` - strategy tests are in `*_test.go` files
674: - **Update both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md** when modifying the strategy to keep documentation current

676: ### `entire review` Command
677: 
678: `entire review` runs a set of configured review skills inside an agent session. The review session is an immutable fact attached to a checkpoint — no verdict, no status tracking, no empty commits. On the next `git commit`, the review session is condensed into the checkpoint metadata alongside normal sessions, permanently recording that the code was reviewed and which skills were run.
679: 
680: #### Command Surface
681: 
682: ```
683: entire review                          # Normal run: load config, run configured agent(s)
684: entire review --edit                   # Re-open the skills picker before running
685: entire review --agent <name>           # Force a specific configured agent (skips multi-picker)
686: entire review attach <session-id>      # Tag an existing agent session as a review (post-hoc)
687: entire review attach --force           # Skip confirmation
688: entire review attach --agent <name>    # Agent that created the session
689: entire review attach --skills <s,...>  # Declare which skills were run
690: ```
691: 
692: When two or more launchable agents are configured and `--agent` is not set, a multi-select picker appears with an optional per-run prompt field (e.g. "focus on security"). Selecting one agent or passing `--agent` runs the single-agent path; selecting two or more runs the N-agent path.
693: 
694: #### Settings Schema
695: 
696: Review skills are configured per-agent in `.entire/settings.json`:
697: 
698: ```json
699: {
700:   "review": {
701:     "claude-code": {"skills": ["/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr"], "prompt": "Be thorough."},
702:     "codex": {"skills": ["/codex:adversarial-review"]}
703:   }
704: }
705: ```
706: 
707: The key is the agent name. The value is a `ReviewConfig` with `skills` (skill invocations passed verbatim to the agent) and optional `prompt` (an always-prompt appended to the composed prompt). Settings field: `EntireSettings.Review` in `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go`.
708: 
709: #### How It Works (env-var handshake)
710: 
711: 1. `entire review` selects the configured agent (override → alphabetically first → prompt if multiple), composes the review prompt via `review.ComposeReviewPrompt`, and computes scope (mainline base ref via `review.ComputeScopeStats`, overridable with `--base`).
712: 2. **For launchable agents** (claude-code, codex, gemini-cli): the spawned agent process is given env vars `ENTIRE_REVIEW_{SESSION,AGENT,SKILLS,PROMPT,STARTING_SHA}` that the agent's `UserPromptSubmit` lifecycle hook reads to tag the session as `Kind = "agent_review"` with the configured skills/prompt. Each spawned process has its own env, so multiple worktrees and multi-agent runs are correct by construction (no shared marker file, no race).
713: 3. **For non-launchable agents** (cursor, opencode, factoryai-droid): `RunMarkerFallback` writes a `PendingReviewMarker` file and prints guidance — the user opens the agent themselves and runs the skills. Single shared file (`review/marker_fallback.go`); adding new non-launchable agents is a registry entry, not a new file.
714: 4. The agent runs the review skills; the session ends naturally.
715: 5. On the next `git commit`, the PostCommit hook condenses the review session into the checkpoint on `entire/checkpoints/v1`, with `Kind` and `ReviewSkills` recorded in `CommittedMetadata`.
716: 6. The `CheckpointSummary` sets `HasReview = true` for O(1) lookup. `HasReview` is an umbrella "any review happened" flag — future review kinds (e.g. manual review) should also set it.
717: 7. `entire status` and the re-run guard read `HasReview` from the checkpoint metadata (no commit history walking).
718: 
719: #### Checkpoint Metadata
720: 
721: Review metadata is stored at two levels on `entire/checkpoints/v1`:
722: 
723: - **`CommittedMetadata` (per-session)**: `kind: "agent_review"`, `review_skills: ["/skill1", "/skill2"]`, `review_prompt: "..."`
724: - **`CheckpointSummary` (per-checkpoint)**: `has_review: true` (umbrella; set when any session in the checkpoint has a review-kind `Kind`)
725: 
726: #### Architecture
727: 
728: - **`AgentReviewer` interface** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/types/reviewer.go`): per-agent contract with `Name() string` and `Start(ctx, RunConfig) (Process, error)`. Each launchable agent implements this in its own package.
729: - **`ReviewerTemplate`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/types/template.go`): shared scaffolding (Spawn → pipe stdout → run parser → forward events → close). Each agent supplies only its `BuildCmd` (argv/env) and `Parser` (stdout-to-Event stream).
730: - **`Sink` interface**: consumers of the event stream. Production sinks: `DumpSink` (post-run per-agent narrative), `TUISink` (Bubble Tea live dashboard with Ctrl+O drill-in), `SynthesisSink` (opt-in y/N cross-agent verdict). Sinks are composed by `composeMultiAgentSinks` based on TTY detection.
731: - **`Run(ctx, reviewer, cfg, sinks)`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/run.go`): single-agent orchestrator. Forwards events to all sinks via `AgentEvent`, calls `RunFinished` once at end with a populated `RunSummary`. Sink dispatch is serialized; sinks need not internally synchronize.
732: - **`RunMulti(ctx, reviewers, cfg, sinks)`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/run_multi.go`): N-agent orchestrator. Each agent runs concurrently in its own goroutine; events fan into a single dispatch loop so the serial-dispatch contract is preserved. Per-agent skills/prompts are injected via `perAgentConfiguredReviewer` adapter (each reviewer sees its own `RunConfig` despite the shared API surface).
733: - **Env-var contract** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/env.go`): single source of truth for `ENTIRE_REVIEW_*` constants used by spawn-side and lifecycle adoption.
734: - **Scope detection** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/scope.go`): `detectScopeBaseRef` returns the first existing ref from the fallback chain `origin/HEAD → origin/main → origin/master → main → master`. Overridable per-invocation via `--base <ref>` (validated through go-git's `ResolveRevision`). Banner output: "Reviewing feat/X vs main: 3 commits, 7 files changed, 2 uncommitted".
735: 
736: #### Multi-Agent UI
737: 
738: When `RunMulti` is dispatched in a TTY, the sink slice is `[TUISink, DumpSink, SynthesisSink?]`:
739: 
740: - **`TUISink` / `reviewTUIModel`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/tui_sink.go`, `tui_model.go`, `tui_detail.go`): live dashboard with one row per agent (name, status, tokens, last assistant preview, duration). `Ctrl+O` enters drill-in mode on the alt screen showing the full event buffer for the selected agent; `Esc` returns to the dashboard. `Ctrl+C` cancels the run via the shared `CancelFunc`. The model uses `tea.WithoutSignalHandler` so the cobra root retains SIGINT routing. After all agents finish, the user dismisses with any key — `RunFinished` blocks on dismissal so `DumpSink` renders below the TUI rather than overlapping it.
741: - **`SynthesisSink`** (`cmd/entire/cli/review/synthesis_sink.go`): opt-in y/N prompt offered after the dump. On "y", composes a synthesis prompt covering all agent narratives + per-run user prompt, calls the configured summary provider, and prints the unified verdict. Skipped silently when stdin can't prompt, the run was cancelled, or fewer than 2 agents produced usable output. Provider failures degrade gracefully ("synthesis unavailable: <err>") so the user can still commit.
742: - **Sink composition** (`composeMultiAgentSinks` in `cmd/entire/cli/review/cmd.go`): pure helper taking explicit `isTTY`/`canPrompt` so tests don't depend on real TTY detection. `findTUISink` picks the TUI out of the slice for `Start`/`Wait` lifecycle hooks.
743: 
744: #### Skill Discovery (Claude Code)
745: 
746: `DiscoverReviewSkills` (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/discovery.go`) walks three roots: plugin cache (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/<market>/<plugin>/<version>/{skills,commands,agents}`), user skills (`~/.claude/skills`), user commands/agents (`~/.claude/commands`, `~/.claude/agents`).
747: 
748: For the plugin cache, `pickLatestVersion` picks ONE version directory per plugin: highest valid semver wins; if no entries parse as semver, the lexicographic max is picked (handles the `unknown` sentinel some plugins ship). Without this, multiple installed versions of a plugin produced duplicate skill entries in the picker and prompt.
749: 
750: #### Anti-Features (do NOT recreate)
751: 
752: The redesign eliminated several constructs from the prior implementation. None should be reintroduced without explicit design:
753: 
754: - `PendingReviewMarker` for launchable agents (env-var handshake makes it unnecessary)
755: - `WorktreePath` field + worktree-scoping logic (env per process eliminates the multi-tenant problem)
756: - `AgentEntries` map on the marker (each agent has its own env)
757: - Marker overwrite tripwire / refuse-attach guard (the bug classes they defended against don't exist)
758: - `--track-only` flag (intentionally removed by #1009)
759: - `--postreview` / `--finalize` / empty review commits / `/entire-review:finish` skill installer
760: - `Launcher` + `HeadlessLauncher` as separate interfaces (single `AgentReviewer`)
761: - `filterCodexOutput` in shared multi-agent code (lives in codex's adapter)
762: - `sync.Once`-guarded onCancel + parallel `signal.Notify` goroutine (single cancel from start)

816:         huh.NewSelect[string]().
817:             Title("Choose an option").
818:             Options(...).
819:             Value(&choice),

832:     huh.NewGroup(
833:         huh.NewConfirm().
834:             Title("Confirm action?").
835:             Value(&confirmed),
836:     ),
837: )
838: if isAccessibleMode() {
839:     form = form.WithAccessible(true)
840: }
841: if err := form.Run(); err != nil { ... }
842: ```

844: ### Key Points
845: 
846: - Always use the accessibility helpers for any `huh` forms/prompts
847: - Test new interactive features with `ACCESSIBLE=1` to ensure they work

148: ## Key Concepts
149: 
150: ### Sessions
151: 
152: A **session** represents a complete interaction with your AI agent, from start to finish. Each session captures all prompts, responses, files modified, and timestamps.
153: 
154: **Session ID format:** `YYYY-MM-DD-<UUID>` (e.g., `2026-01-08-abc123de-f456-7890-abcd-ef1234567890`)
155: 
156: Sessions are stored separately from your code commits on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
157: 
158: ### Checkpoints
159: 
160: A **checkpoint** is a snapshot within a session that you can rewind to—a "save point" in your work.
161: 
162: Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit. **Checkpoint IDs** are 12-character hex strings (e.g., `a3b2c4d5e6f7`).
163: 
164: ### How It Works
165: 
166: ```
167: Your Branch                    entire/checkpoints/v1
168:      │                                  │
169:      ▼                                  │
170: [Base Commit]                           │
171:      │                                  │
172:      │  ┌─── Agent works ───┐           │
173:      │  │  Step 1           │           │
174:      │  │  Step 2           │           │
175:      │  │  Step 3           │           │
176:      │  └───────────────────┘           │
177:      │                                  │
178:      ▼                                  ▼
179: [Your Commit] ─────────────────► [Session Metadata]
180:      │                           (transcript, prompts,
181:      │                            files touched)
182:      ▼
183: ```
184: 
185: Checkpoints are saved as you work. When you commit, session metadata is permanently stored on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch and linked to your commit.
186: 
187: ### Strategy
188: 
189: Entire uses a manual-commit strategy that keeps your git history clean:
190: 
191: - **No commits on your branch** — Entire never creates commits on the active branch
192: - **Safe on any branch** — works on main, master, and feature branches alike
193: - **Non-destructive rewind** — restore files from any checkpoint without altering commit history
194: - **Metadata stored separately** — all session data lives on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch
195: 
196: ### Git Worktrees
197: 
198: Entire works seamlessly with [git worktrees](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree). Each worktree has independent session tracking, so you can run multiple AI sessions in different worktrees without conflicts.

201: 
202: Multiple AI sessions can run on the same commit. If you start a second session while another has uncommitted work, Entire warns you and tracks them separately. Both sessions' checkpoints are preserved and can be rewound independently.

313: ## Configuration
314: 
315: Entire uses two configuration files in the `.entire/` directory:
316: 
317: ### settings.json (Project Settings)
318: 
319: Shared across the team, typically committed to git:
320: 
321: ```json
322: {
323:   "enabled": true
324: }
325: ```
326: 
327: ### settings.local.json (Local Settings)
328: 
329: Personal overrides, gitignored by default:
330: 
331: ```json
332: {
333:   "enabled": false,
334:   "log_level": "debug"
335: }
336: ```
337: 
338: ### Configuration Options
339: 
340: | Option                               | Values                                       | Description                                             |
341: | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
342: | `enabled`                            | `true`, `false`                              | Enable/disable Entire                                   |
343: | `log_level`                          | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`             | Logging verbosity                                       |
344: | `strategy_options.push_sessions`     | `true`, `false`                              | Auto-push `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch on git push    |
345: | `strategy_options.checkpoint_remote` | `{"provider": "github", "repo": "org/repo"}` | Push checkpoint branches to a separate repo (see below) |
346: | `strategy_options.summarize.enabled` | `true`, `false`                              | Auto-generate AI summaries at commit time               |
347: | `telemetry`                          | `true`, `false`                              | Send anonymous usage statistics to Posthog              |
348: 
349: ### Agent Hook Configuration
350: 
351: Each agent stores its hook configuration in its own directory. When you run `entire enable`, hooks are installed in the appropriate location for each selected agent:
352: 
353: | Agent            | Hook Location                 | Format            |
354: | ---------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------- |
355: | Claude Code      | `.claude/settings.json`       | JSON hooks config |
356: | Codex            | `.codex/hooks.json`           | JSON hooks config |
357: | Copilot CLI      | `.github/hooks/entire.json`   | JSON hooks config |
358: | Cursor           | `.cursor/hooks.json`          | JSON hooks config |
359: | Factory AI Droid | `.factory/settings.json`      | JSON hooks config |
360: | Gemini CLI       | `.gemini/settings.json`       | JSON hooks config |
361: | OpenCode         | `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` | TypeScript plugin |
362: 
363: You can enable multiple agents at the same time — each agent's hooks are independent. Entire detects which agents are active by checking for installed hooks, not by a setting in `settings.json`.
364: 
365: ### Checkpoint Remote
366: 
367: By default, Entire pushes `entire/checkpoints/v1` to the same remote as your code. If you want to push checkpoint data to a separate repo (e.g., a private repo for public projects), configure `checkpoint_remote` with a structured provider and repo:
368: 
369: ```json
370: {
371:   "strategy_options": {
372:     "checkpoint_remote": {
373:       "provider": "github",
374:       "repo": "myorg/checkpoints-private"
375:     }
376:   }
377: }
378: ```
379: 
380: Or via the CLI:
381: 
382: ```bash
383: entire enable --checkpoint-remote github:myorg/checkpoints-private
384: ```
385: 
386: Entire derives the git URL automatically using the same protocol (SSH or HTTPS) as your push remote. It will:
387: 
388: - Fetch the checkpoint branch locally if it exists on the remote but not locally (one-time)
389: - Push `entire/checkpoints/v1` to the checkpoint repo instead of your default push remote
390: - Skip pushing if a fork is detected (push remote owner differs from checkpoint repo owner)
391: - If the remote is unreachable, warn and continue without blocking your main push
392: 
393: #### `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN`
394: 
395: `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINT_TOKEN` allows you to provide a dedicated token for checkpoint repository operations, without modifying the credentials used for your primary repository.
396: 
397: When this environment variable is set, Entire behaves as follows:
398: 
399: - Injects the token into HTTPS Git operations used for checkpoint fetch and push
400: - If `checkpoint_remote` is configured:
401:   - Prefers an HTTPS URL for the checkpoint remote when a token is present, even if the repository’s `origin` uses SSH
402: - If `checkpoint_remote` is not configured:
403:   - Falls back to using the default `origin` remote
404: - If `checkpoint_remote` configuration cannot be loaded:
405:   - Falls back to `origin`
406:   - If `origin` is a valid SSH or HTTPS Git remote, Entire converts it to an HTTPS URL to enable token-based authentication
407: 
408: ### Auto-Summarization
409: 
410: When enabled, Entire automatically generates AI summaries for checkpoints at commit time. Summaries capture intent, outcome, learnings, friction points, and open items from the session.
411: 
412: ```json
413: {
414:   "strategy_options": {
415:     "summarize": {
416:       "enabled": true
417:     }
418:   }
419: }
420: ```
421: 
422: **Requirements:**
423: 
424: - Claude CLI must be installed and authenticated (`claude` command available in PATH)
425: - Summary generation is non-blocking: failures are logged but don't prevent commits
426: 
427: **Note:** Currently uses Claude CLI for summary generation. Other AI backends may be supported in future versions.
428: 
429: ### Settings Priority
430: 
431: Local settings override project settings field-by-field. When you run `entire status`, it shows both project and local (effective) settings.
432: 
433: ### Agent-Specific Steps & Limitations
434: 
435: - When enabling Entire for Codex, the command will also create or update `.codex/config.toml` with `codex_hooks = true` to enable Codex hooks. If you configure Codex manually, make sure this flag is set in your `.codex/config.toml`. Or select Codex from the interactive agent picker when running `entire enable`.
436: - Entire supports Cursor IDE and Cursor Agent CLI tool, but `entire rewind` is not available at this time. Other commands (`doctor`, `status` etc.) work the same as all other agents.
437: - Entire supports Copilot CLI, but not Copilot in VS Code, in other IDEs, or on github.com.
438: 
439: ## Security & Privacy
440: 
441: **Your session transcripts are stored in your git repository** on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. If your repository is public, this data is visible to anyone.
442: 
443: Entire automatically redacts detected secrets (API keys, tokens, credentials) when writing to `entire/checkpoints/v1`, but redaction is best-effort. Temporary shadow branches used during a session may contain unredacted data and should not be pushed. See [docs/security-and-privacy.md](docs/security-and-privacy.md) for details.
444: 
445: ## Troubleshooting
446: 
447: ### Common Issues
448: 
449: | Issue                    | Solution                                                |
450: | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
451: | "Not a git repository"   | Navigate to a Git repository first                      |
452: | "Entire is disabled"     | Run `entire enable`                                     |
453: | "No rewind points found" | Work with your configured agent and commit your changes |
454: | "shadow branch conflict" | Run `entire clean --force`                              |
455: 
456: ### SSH Authentication Errors
457: 
458: If you see an error like this when running `entire resume`:
459: 
460: ```
461: Failed to fetch metadata: failed to fetch entire/checkpoints/v1 from origin: ssh: handshake failed: ssh: unable to authenticate, attempted methods [none publickey], no supported methods remain
462: ```
463: 
464: This is a [known issue with go-git's SSH handling](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/issues/411). Fix it by adding GitHub's host keys to your known_hosts file:
465: 
466: ```
467: ssh-keyscan -t rsa github.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts
468: ssh-keyscan -t ecdsa github.com >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts
469: ```
470: 
471: ### Debug Mode
472: 
473: ```
474: # Via environment variable
475: ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug entire status
476:

478: {

483: ### Cleaning Up State
484: 
485: ```
486: # Clean session data for current commit
487: entire clean --force
488: 
489: # Clean all orphaned data across the repository
490: entire clean --all --force
491: 
492: # Disable and re-enable
493: entire disable && entire enable --force
494: ```

496: ### Accessibility
497: 
498: For screen reader users, enable accessible mode:
499: 
500: ```
501: export ACCESSIBLE=1
502: entire enable
503: ```
504: 
505: This uses simpler text prompts instead of interactive TUI elements.

507: ## Development
508: 
509: This project uses [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) for task automation and dependency management.
510: 
511: ### Prerequisites
512: 
513: - [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) - Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`
514: 
515: ### Getting Started
516: 
517: ```
518: # Clone the repository
519: git clone <repo-url>
520: cd cli
521: 
522: # Install dependencies (including Go)
523: mise install
524: 
525: # Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
526: mise trust
527: 
528: # Build the CLI
529: mise run build
530: ```
531: 
532: ### Dev Container
533: 
534: The repo includes a `.devcontainer/` configuration that installs the system packages used by local development and CI (`git`, `tmux`, `gnome-keyring`, etc) and then bootstraps the repo's `mise` toolchain.
535: 
536: Open the folder in a Dev Container, or start it from the `devcontainer` CLI as follows:
537: 
538: ```bash
539: devcontainer up --workspace-folder .
540: devcontainer exec --workspace-folder . bash -lc '.devcontainer/run-with-keyring.sh'
541: ```
542: 
543: The container's `postCreateCommand` runs `mise trust --yes && mise install`, so Go, `golangci-lint`, `gotestsum`, `shellcheck`, and the canary E2E helper binaries are ready after creation. Use `.devcontainer/run-with-keyring.sh <command>` for commands that touch the Linux keyring, including `mise run test:ci`.
544: 
545: If `ENTIRE_DEVCONTAINER_KEYRING_PASSWORD` is set in the environment, `.devcontainer/run-with-keyring.sh` uses that value to unlock the keyring non-interactively. If it is unset, the script generates a random password for the session automatically.
546: 
547: ### Common Tasks
548: 
549: ```
550: # Run tests
551: mise run test
552: 
553: # Run integration tests
554: mise run test:integration
555: 
556: # Run all tests (unit + integration, CI mode)
557: mise run test:ci
558: 
559: # Lint the code
560: mise run lint
561: 
562: # Format the code
563: mise run fmt
564: ```

1: # Security Policy
2: 
3: We take security seriously at Entire. We appreciate your efforts to responsibly disclose vulnerabilities and will make every effort to acknowledge your contributions.
4: 
5: ## Reporting a Vulnerability
6: 
7: **Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.**
8: 
9: Instead, please send security-related reports to **[security@entire.io](mailto:security@entire.io)**.
10: 
11: ### What to Include
12: 
13: When reporting a vulnerability, please include:
14: 
15: 1. **Description** - A clear description of the vulnerability
16: 2. **Impact** - What an attacker could achieve by exploiting this issue
17: 3. **Steps to reproduce** - Detailed steps to reproduce the vulnerability
18: 4. **Affected versions** - Which versions of the CLI are affected (if known)
19: 5. **Suggested fix** - If you have ideas on how to fix it (optional)
20: 
21: ### What to Expect
22: 
23: - **Acknowledgment** - We will acknowledge receipt of your report within 48 hours
24: - **Updates** - We will keep you informed of our progress as we investigate
25: - **Resolution** - We aim to resolve critical vulnerabilities within 90 days
26: 
27: ## Confidentiality
28: 
29: **All reports will be kept confidential.** We will not share your information with third parties without your consent, except as required by law.
30: 
31: ## Supported Versions
32: 
33: We recommend always running the latest version of the Entire CLI.
34: 
35: ## Scope
36: 
37: This security policy applies to:
38: 
39: - The Entire CLI (`entire` command-line tool)
40: - Official Entire GitHub repositories
41: - Entire-related services at entire.io
42: 
43: ### Out of Scope
44: 
45: The following are generally not considered security vulnerabilities:
46: 
47: - Issues in third-party dependencies (please report these upstream)
48: - Social engineering attacks
49: - Denial of service attacks
50: - Issues requiring physical access to a user's device
51: 
52: ---
53: 
54: ## Security Advisories
55: 
56: Security advisories are issued when a confirmed vulnerability can be exploited by a remote or non-local actor. Because the Entire CLI is primarily used as a local development tool, the following are generally treated as **bug reports rather than security advisories**:
57: 
58: - Regular expression performance issues (ReDoS) that only affect local execution
59: - Resource exhaustion that requires local access to trigger
60: - Issues that cannot be exploited without direct access to the user's machine
61: 
62: Use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) to report bugs.
63: 
64: ---
65: 
66: Thank you for helping keep Entire and our community safe!
67: 

(End of file - total 67 lines)
</content>

1: # Code of Conduct
2: 
3: 
4: We're committed to providing a welcoming, respectful, and harassment-free environment for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.
5: 
6: ## Scope
7: 
8: This Code of Conduct applies to all Entire community spaces, including:
9: 
10: - **GitHub** - repositories, issues, pull requests, discussions, and comments
11: - **Discord** - all channels in the Entire workspace
12: - **Events** - meetups, conferences, and online gatherings hosted by Entire
13: - **Public representation** - acting as a representative of Entire in public spaces, including social media, forums, and conferences
14: 
15: This Code of Conduct also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces.
16: 
17: ## Expected Behavior
18: 
19: - **Be respectful** - Treat everyone professionally, listen actively, and be mindful of your words
20: - **Be inclusive** - Use inclusive language and make space for everyone to contribute
21: - **Be collaborative** - Help each other, share knowledge, and celebrate wins together
22: - **Be accountable** - Own your mistakes, follow through on commitments, and take responsibility for your impact
23: - **Be empathetic** - Try to understand different perspectives and experiences
24: - **Give and accept constructive feedback gracefully**
25: 
26: ## Unacceptable Behavior
27: 
28: This includes but isn't limited to:
29: 
30: - Harassment, discrimination, or offensive comments related to personal characteristics
31: - Personal attacks, trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, or deliberate intimidation
32: - Unwelcome sexual attention, advances, or imagery
33: - Sharing private information (such as physical or email addresses) without explicit consent
34: - Sustained disruption of discussions or events
35: - Advocating for or encouraging any of the above behavior
36: - Conduct that could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting
37: 
38: ## Reporting
39: 
40: To report a Code of Conduct violation, contact **[conduct@entire.io](mailto:conduct@entire.io)**.
41: 
42: For security vulnerabilities, please email **[security@entire.io](mailto:security@entire.io)** instead. See our [Security Policy](SECURITY.md).
43: 
44: ### Confidentiality
45: 
46: **All reports will be kept confidential.** We will not share your identity or the details of your report with anyone outside the enforcement team without your consent, except as required by law or to protect safety.
47: 
48: ### What to Include
49: 
50: - Your contact information (so we can follow up)
51: - Names of those involved (or identifying information)
52: - Description of the behavior and when/where it occurred
53: - Any additional context or evidence (screenshots, links)
54: - Whether you would like to remain anonymous to the reported party
55: 
56: ## Enforcement
57: 
58: Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing standards of acceptable behavior. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.
59: 
60: Violations will be addressed according to their severity and frequency:
61: 
62: #### 1. Correction
63: **For:** First-time minor violations or misunderstandings
64: 
65: **Action:** A private, written notice explaining the violation and why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: #### 2. Warning
70: **For:** A single incident or pattern of minor violations
71: 
72: **Action:** A formal warning with consequences for continued behavior. This includes no interaction with the people involved for a specified period. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: #### 3. Temporary Ban
77: **For:** Serious violations or sustained inappropriate behavior
78: 
79: **Action:** A temporary ban from all community interaction and public communication for a specified period (typically 30-90 days). No public or private interaction with the community is permitted during this time.
80: 
81: ---
82: 
83: #### 4. Permanent Ban
84: **For:** Demonstrating a pattern of violations, severe harassment, or aggression toward individuals or groups
85: 
86: **Action:** Permanent removal from all community spaces. This decision is final.
87: 
88: ---
89: 
90: ## Attribution
91: 
92: This Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/), version 2.1.
93: 
94: For answers to common questions about the Contributor Covenant, see the [FAQ](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq).

1: # Contributing to the Entire CLI
2: 
3: Thank you for your interest in contributing to Entire! We welcome contributions from everyone.
4: 
5: Please read our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before participating.
6: 
7: > **New to Entire?** See the [README](README.md) for setup and usage documentation.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## Before You Code: Discuss First
12: 
13: The fastest way to get a contribution merged is to align with maintainers before writing code. Please **open an issue first** using our [issue templates](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/new/choose) and wait for maintainer feedback before starting implementation.
14: 
15: ### Contribution Workflow
16: 
17: 1. **Open an issue** describing the problem or feature
18: 2. **Wait for maintainer feedback** -- we may have relevant context or plans
19: 3. **Get approval** before starting implementation
20: 4. **Submit your PR** referencing the approved issue
21: 5. **Address all feedback** including automated Copilot comments
22: 6. **Maintainer review and merge**
23: 
24: ---
25: 
26: ## First-Time Contributors
27: 
28: New to the project? Welcome! Here's how to get started:
29: 
30: ### Good First Issues
31: 
32: We recommend starting with:
33: - **Documentation improvements** - Fix typos, clarify explanations, add examples
34: - **Test contributions** - Add test cases, improve coverage
35: - **Small bug fixes** - Issues labeled `good-first-issue`
36: 
37: ---
38: 
39: ## Submitting Issues
40: 
41: All feature requests, bug reports, and general issues should be submitted through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues). Please search for existing issues before opening a new one.
42: 
43: For security-related issues, see the Security section below.
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ## Security
48: 
49: If you discover a security vulnerability, **do not report it through GitHub Issues**. Instead, please follow the instructions in our [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) file for responsible disclosure. All security reports are kept confidential as described in SECURITY.md.
50: 
51: ---
52: 
53: ## Contributions & Communication
54: 
55: Contributions and communications are expected to occur through:
56: 
57: - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) - Bug reports and feature requests
58: - [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) - Questions, general conversation, and real-time support
59: 
60: Please represent the project and community respectfully in all public and private interactions.
61: 
62: 
63: ## How to Contribute
64: 
65: 
66: There are many ways to contribute:
67: 
68: - **Feature requests** - Open a [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) to discuss your idea
69: - **Bug reports** - Report issues via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) (see [Reporting Bugs](#reporting-bugs))
70: - **Code contributions** - Fix bugs, add features, improve tests
71: - **Documentation** - Improve guides, fix typos, add examples
72: - **Community** - Help others, answer questions, share knowledge
73: 
74: 
75: ## Reporting Bugs
76: 
77: Good bug reports help us fix issues quickly. When reporting a bug, please include:
78: 
79: ### Required Information
80: 
81: 1. **Entire CLI version** - run `entire version`
82: 2. **Operating system**
83: 3. **Go version** - run `go version`
84: 
85: ### What to Include
86: 
87: Please answer these questions in your bug report:
88: 
89: 1. **What did you do?** - Include the exact commands you ran
90: 2. **What did you expect to happen?**
91: 3. **What actually happened?** - Include the full error message or unexpected output
92: 4. **Can you reproduce it?** - Does it happen every time or intermittently?
93: 5. **Any additional context?** - Logs, screenshots, or related issues
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## Local Setup
98: 
99: ### Prerequisites
100: 
101: - **Go 1.26.x** - Check with `go version`
102: - **mise** - Task runner and version manager. Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`
103: 
104: ### Clone and Install
105: 
106: ```bash
107: # Clone the repository
108: git clone https://github.com/entireio/cli.git
109: cd cli
110: 
111: # Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
112: mise trust
113: 
114: # Install dependencies (mise will install the correct Go version)
115: mise install
116: 
117: # Download Go modules
118: go mod download
119: 
120: # Build the CLI
121: mise run build
122: 
123: # Verify setup by running tests
124: mise run test
125: ```
126: 
127: > See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for detailed architecture and development reference.
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ## Making Changes
132: 
133: 1. **Create a branch** for your changes:
134:    ```bash
135:    git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
136:    ```
137: 
138: 2. **Make your changes** - follow the [Code Style](#code-style) guidelines
139: 
140: 3. **Test your changes** - see [Testing](#testing)
141: 
142: 4. **Commit** with clear, descriptive messages:
143:    ```bash
144:    git commit -m "Add feature: description of what you added"
145:    ```
146: 
147: ---
148: 
149: ## Code Style
150: 
151: Follow standard Go idioms and conventions. For detailed guidance, see the **Go Code Style** section in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).
152: 
153: ### Key Points
154: 
155: - **Error handling**: Handle all errors explicitly - don't leave them unchecked
156: - **Formatting**: Code must pass `gofmt` (run `mise run fmt`)
157: - **Linting**: Code must pass `golangci-lint` (run `mise run lint`)
158: - **Naming**: Use meaningful, descriptive names following Go conventions
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: ## Testing
163: 
164: > See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for complete testing documentation.
165: 
166: ```bash
167: # Unit tests - always run before committing
168: mise run test
169: 
170: # Integration tests
171: mise run test:integration
172: 
173: # Full CI suite
174: mise run test:ci
175: ```
176: 
177: Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## Creating an Agent
182: 
183: 
184: Entire supports two ways to create agents:
185: 
186: ### 1. Claude Code Agent Personas (Markdown)
187: 
188: These are markdown files that define specialized behaviors for Claude Code (e.g., developer, reviewer, etc.).
189: 
190: - **Location:** `.claude/agents/`
191: - **Structure:**
192:    ```markdown
193:    ---
194:    name: my-agent
195:    description: What this agent does
196:    model: opus
197:    color: blue
198:    ---
199: 
200:    # Agent Name
201:    You are a **[Role]** with expertise in [domain].
202: 
203:    ## Core Principles
204:    - Principle 1
205:    - Principle 2
206: 
207:    ## Process
208:    1. Step 1
209:    2. Step 2
210: 
211:    ## Output Format
212:    How to structure responses...
213:    ```
214: - **To invoke:** Create a matching command in `.claude/commands/` that spawns the agent via the Task tool.
215: - **Examples:**
216:    - `.claude/agents/dev.md` - TDD Developer
217:    - `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` - Code Reviewer
218: 
219: ### 2. Coding Agent Integrations (Go)
220: 
221: These are Go implementations that integrate Entire with different AI coding tools (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, etc.) using the Agent abstraction layer.
222: 
223: - **Location:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/`
224: - **Steps:**
225:    1. Implement the `Agent` interface in `agent/agent.go`
226:    2. Register your agent in the agent registry
227:    3. Add setup and hook configuration as needed
228:    4. Ensure session and checkpoint tracking is handled per the abstraction
229: - **Reference:** See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for architecture and code examples.
230: 
231: ---
232: 
233: **Which should I use?**
234: 
235: - Use a persona markdown agent if you want to create a new role or workflow for Claude Code.
236: - Use a coding agent integration if you want to add support for a new AI coding tool or extend agent capabilities in the CLI.
237: 
238: ---
239: 
240: ## Submitting a Pull Request
241: 
242: ### Before You Submit
243: 
244: - **Related issue exists and is approved** -- Your PR references an issue where a maintainer has acknowledged the approach. (Exceptions: documentation fixes, typo corrections, and `good-first-issue` items.)
245: - **Linting passes** -- Run `mise run lint` (includes golangci-lint, gofmt, gomod, shellcheck)
246: - **Tests pass** -- Run `mise run test` to verify your changes
247: - **Tests included** -- New Go code and functionality should have accompanying tests
248: - **Entire checkpoint trailers included** -- See [Using Entire While Contributing](#using-entire-while-contributing) below
249: 
250: PRs that skip these steps are likely to be closed without merge.
251: 
252: ### Submitting
253: 
254: 1. **Push** your branch to your fork
255: 2. **Open a PR** against the `main` branch
256: 3. **Describe your changes** -- Link the related issue, summarize what changed and what testing you did
257: 4. **Address Copilot feedback** -- See [Responding to Automated Review](#responding-to-automated-review)
258: 5. **Wait for maintainer review**
259: 
260: ---
261: 
262: ## Responding to Automated Review
263: 
264: Co-pilot agent reviews every PR and provides feedback on code quality, potential bugs, and project conventions.
265: 
266: **Read and respond to every Copilot comment.** PRs with unaddressed Copilot feedback will not move to maintainer review.
267: 
268: - **Fixed** -- Push a commit addressing the issue.
269: - **Disagree** -- Reply explaining your reasoning. The Copilot isn't always right.
270: - **Question** -- Ask for clarification. We're happy to help.
271: 
272: Addressing Copilot feedback upfront is the fastest path to maintainer review.
273: 
274: ---
275: 
276: ## Using Entire While Contributing
277: 
278: We use Entire on Entire. When contributing, install the Entire CLI and let it capture your coding sessions -- this gives us valuable dogfooding data and helps improve the tool.
279: 
280: ### Setup
281: 
282: Install the latest version of the Entire CLI (see [installation docs](https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation)) and verify with `entire version`. Entire is already configured in this repository, so there's no need to run `entire enable`.
283: 
284: ### Checkpoint Trailers
285: 
286: All commits should include `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers from your sessions. These are added automatically by the `prepare-commit-msg` hook when Entire is enabled. The trailers link your commits to session metadata on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch.
287: 
288: ### Sessions Branch
289: 
290: When you push your PR branch, Entire can automatically push the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch alongside it (if `push_sessions` is enabled in your settings). Include this in your PR so maintainers can review the session context behind your changes.
291: 
292: ---
293: 
294: ## Troubleshooting
295: 
296: ### Common Setup Issues
297: 
298: **`go mod download` fails with timeout**
299: ```bash
300: # Try using direct mode
301: GOPROXY=direct go mod download
302: ```
303: 
304: **`mise install` fails**
305: ```bash
306: # Ensure mise is properly installed
307: curl https://mise.run | sh
308: 
309: # Reload your shell
310: source ~/.zshrc  # or ~/.bashrc
311: ```
312: 
313: **Binary not updating after rebuild**
314: ```bash
315: # Check which binary is being used

1: # Windows Support
2: 
3: ## Prerequisites
4: 
5: - **Windows 10 1809+** (required for ConPTY support in E2E tests)
6: - **Git for Windows** — provides `git.exe` and bundled bash for git hooks
7: - **Go 1.26+** — for building from source
8: 
9: ## Building
10: 
11: Cross-compile from macOS/Linux:
12: 
13: ```bash
14: mise run build:windows          # amd64
15: mise run build:windows-arm64    # arm64
16: ```
17: 
18: Or build natively on Windows:
19: 
20: ```bash
21: go build -o entire.exe ./cmd/entire/
22: ```
23: 
24: ## Installation
25: 
26: Copy `entire.exe` to a directory in your `PATH`. Git for Windows must be installed and available in `PATH`.
27: 
28: ## How It Works
29: 
30: The CLI is pure Go with no CGO dependencies, so cross-compilation produces a fully static binary.
31: 
32: ### Git Hooks
33: 
34: Git hooks use `#!/bin/sh` shebangs with POSIX shell syntax. Git for Windows executes hooks through its bundled MSYS2 bash, so they work as-is. No batch file wrappers are needed.
35: 
36: ### Agent Hooks
37: 
38: Agent-specific hooks (Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode) are JSON configuration — the agents themselves handle execution. The hooks call `entire.exe` directly via `exec.Command`, not through a shell.
39: 
40: ## Testing
41: 
42: ### Unit + Integration Tests
43: 
44: ```bash
45: go test ./...                                          # unit tests
46: go test -tags=integration ./cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/...  # integration tests
47: go test -tags=integration -race ./...                  # all (CI equivalent)
48: ```
49: 
50: ### E2E Tests
51: 
52: E2E tests require the agent binary (e.g., `claude`) to be installed and available in `PATH`.
53: 
54: ```bash
55: # Set required env vars
56: set E2E_ENTIRE_BIN=entire.exe
57: set E2E_AGENT=claude-code        # or gemini-cli, opencode
58: 
59: # Run all E2E tests
60: go test -tags=e2e -count=1 -timeout=30m ./e2e/tests/...
61: 
62: # Run a specific test
63: go test -tags=e2e -count=1 -timeout=30m -run TestSingleSessionManualCommit ./e2e/tests/...
64: ```
65: 
66: The E2E test infrastructure uses native PTY (ConPTY on Windows, creack/pty on Unix) instead of tmux, so no tmux installation is needed.
67: 
68: ## Known Limitations
69: 
70: - **Interactive integration tests** that use PTY (`resume_interactive_test.go`) are skipped on Windows (guarded with `//go:build unix`).
71: - **File permissions** (0o755, 0o644) are set but ignored by Windows — Windows uses ACLs instead.
72: - **Symlinks** in E2E tests require Windows Developer Mode or admin privileges.
73: - **OpenCode plugin** uses `Bun.spawnSync(["sh", "-c", ...])` which won't work on Windows unless Bun supports it. OpenCode Windows support is pending.
74: 
75: ## Smoke Test Checklist
76: 
77: After building, verify these work on a Windows machine:
78: 
79: 1. `entire.exe version`
80: 2. `entire.exe enable` — in a git repo with an agent installed
81: 3. Start an agent session, make file changes
82: 4. `git add . && git commit -m "test"` — hooks should fire (prepare-commit-msg, post-commit)
83: 5. `entire.exe rewind --list` — should show checkpoint(s)
84: 6. `entire.exe explain` — pager should use `more` by default
85: 
86: ## Architecture Notes
87: 
88: ### Platform-Specific Files
89: 
90: | File | Purpose |
91: |------|---------|
92: | `cmd/entire/cli/telemetry/detached_unix.go` | Telemetry subprocess via `Setpgid` |
93: | `cmd/entire/cli/telemetry/detached_windows.go` | Telemetry subprocess via `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` |
94: | `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/procattr_unix.go` | Test process detachment via `Setsid` |
95: | `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/procattr_windows.go` | Test process detachment via `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` |
96: | `e2e/agents/procattr_unix.go` | E2E process groups via `Setpgid` + `SIGKILL` |
97: | `e2e/agents/procattr_windows.go` | E2E process groups via `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` |
98: | `e2e/agents/pty_session_unix.go` | Interactive E2E sessions via `creack/pty` |
99: | `e2e/agents/pty_session_windows.go` | Interactive E2E sessions via ConPTY |
100: 
101: ### Cross-Platform Patterns Used
102: 
103: - `os.Interrupt` only (no `syscall.SIGTERM`) for signal handling
104: - `filepath.FromSlash()` on git CLI output paths
105: - `strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\r\n", "\n")` for CRLF-safe git output parsing
106: - `os.DevNull` instead of hardcoded `/dev/null`
107: - `runtime.GOOS == "windows"` for pager selection (`more` vs `less`)
108: - Build-tagged `_unix.go` / `_windows.go` files for syscall differences

(End of file - total 108 lines)
